about: The Lubavitch centres of about 1984, as American Friends of Lubavitch listed them: 'On the following pages we are sharing with you information of the addresses of Lubavitcher Centers in their respective states.' The booklet says 'Eighty-two Centers in Thirty-four of the states'; its list has 105 entries in 30 states (schools, camps and offices at a centre's address listed apart), and leaves out metropolitan New York and Canada. Read from the page images (Nov 9 2026), not the PDF's text layer, which garbles several lines. Each entry: state, name and street as printed (spelling kept, 'Berkley' and 'Orrington St.' as printed), city, the PDF page, lat/lon from OpenStreetMap's geocoder ('located': by the street address, or by the town only where the address was not found), and 'today': the centre in today's directory (web/data/centers.geojson) that is the same institution ('link': 'same'), carries on its work without being the same organization ('successor'), or stands in the same building ('building'); for 'same', 'place' says whether today's listing is at the same place (within 400 m of the 1984 address), has moved, or was not checked (the 1984 address not found). 'today' is null where nothing in today's directory matches. Matches by name, director and address; those marked 'probably' in the note are less sure.

source.title: American Friends of Lubavitch booklet on the Rebbe (Reagan Library, Max Green files, folder 'Lubavitch (1 of 2)'), its list of centres
source.note: Made after the National Scroll of Honor (24 March 1983); its list has Oregon's centre (opened Jan 1984) but not Kentucky's (Mar 1985). Its map of who covered which state: work/shetach-history/README.md, 'The 1984 map'.
